title: WebSocket wrappers
what: Reconnect, backoff and send buffers over a plain WebSocket.

title: Realtime protocols with fallbacks
what: Protocols that emulate a socket over WebSocket, streams and polling, as SockJS does.

title: Message brokers
what: Broker protocols over WebSocket: MQTT, STOMP, AMQP, NATS and others.

title: RPC
what: Calls to a server or to another frame: gRPC-Web, Connect, JSON-RPC, tRPC and others.

title: GraphQL
what: Queries over HTTP, and subscriptions over WebSocket or SSE.

title: Streaming over plain HTTP
what: Server-sent events, streamed JSON and multipart responses.

title: Media and WebRTC
what: Peer connections, media servers, WHIP and WHEP, and HTTP video.

title: Chat, social and telephony
what: XMPP, SIP, Matrix, IRC, Nostr and the social APIs.

title: Remote desktop and terminals
what: VNC, Guacamole and terminals over WebSocket.

title: Peer-to-peer and decentralized
what: libp2p, IPFS, BitTorrent and the JSON-RPC of blockchains.

title: Sync and collaboration
what: CRDT and operational-transform sync, replication and sync engines.

title: Databases over HTTP or WebSocket
what: Database protocols that a page can speak.

title: Other HTTP protocols
what: Uploads, object stores, WebDAV, JMAP, OTLP and DNS over HTTPS.

title: IoT, robotics and tools
what: Robot, device and tool protocols over WebSocket.

title: Wire formats
what: Codecs that the protocols carry. They are not transports.
